open_points.subject: answer_request handling of non-tools/call requests
open_points.text: answer_request: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST check one request in exactly this order, the first failure deciding: the byte length of request_bytes is within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SURFACE_REQUEST_BYTES_MAX constant, else invalid_request; authenticate_token with presented_token gives an Actor, else unauthorized with one fixed reason that reveals nothing about any record; the message names a catalogue operation and fits that operation's request model with no unknown field — a field typed X | None fitting when it is absent or JSON null — and every bound below, else invalid_request; the actor may call that operation by the actor table, else not_permitted; only then is the operation's handler called (A16 rule 1).
open_points.other_text: answer_request: [BEHAVIOR] The body is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message, read only after the size and token checks. A JSON object whose jsonrpc is "2.0" with a string method and an id is a request; one with a method and no id is a notification and one with no method a response: both are answered with empty bytes and change nothing. A request's method decides: initialize answers the result {protocolVersion: the imported MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION constant, capabilities: {tools: {listChanged: false}}, serverInfo: {name: the imported MCP_SERVER_NAME constant, version: the imported MCP_SERVER_VERSION constant}} whatever version its params ask, and keeps no state; ping answers an empty result object; tools/list answers {tools: [...]} as below, ignoring any cursor; tools/call names the catalogue operation in params.name and carries its request in params.arguments, which then pass the remaining checks of the first note.
open_points.question: Must every JSON-RPC request name and invoke a catalogue operation, or are initialize, ping and tools/list handled without satisfying that requirement?

open_points.subject: answer_request handling of notifications and responses before authentication
open_points.text: answer_request: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST check one request in exactly this order, the first failure deciding: the byte length of request_bytes is within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SURFACE_REQUEST_BYTES_MAX constant, else invalid_request; authenticate_token with presented_token gives an Actor, else unauthorized with one fixed reason that reveals nothing about any record; the message names a catalogue operation and fits that operation's request model with no unknown field — a field typed X | None fitting when it is absent or JSON null — and every bound below, else invalid_request; the actor may call that operation by the actor table, else not_permitted; only then is the operation's handler called (A16 rule 1).
open_points.other_text: A JSON object whose jsonrpc is "2.0" with a string method and an id is a request; one with a method and no id is a notification and one with no method a response: both are answered with empty bytes and change nothing.
open_points.question: When a notification or response has a missing or invalid token, must authentication produce an unauthorized response as the first failure, or must the message always produce empty bytes and change nothing?

open_points.subject: answer_request response id for failures before the body may be read
open_points.text: answer_request: [FIELD_PROJECTION] The id of every response is the body's id member when the body is one JSON object whose id is a string or an integer, and null otherwise; reading it checks nothing and decides nothing.
open_points.other_text: answer_request: [BEHAVIOR] The body is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message, read only after the size and token checks.
open_points.question: For an oversized or unauthorized body containing a string or integer id, may the body be read to copy that id, or must it remain unread and the response use null?
